 Italy hails youthful Formula 1 champion Kimi Antonelli

 Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli celebrates with this team after clinching the 2026 Formula One World Championship. (Photo: Reuters/Eloisa Sanchez)

 ROME: Italians on Monday (Nov 2) celebrated the success of Kimi Antonelli, who became Formula 1's youngest world champion at the age of 20 when he clinched the title in Mexico City.
 Antonelli, who is from the northern city of Bologna, is also the first Italian champion since 1953.
 Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni took to social media to praise what she called an "extraordinary achievement".
 "A success that puts an Italian driver back on top of the world, rewarding talent, commitment, determination and dedication," Meloni said.

 "It's a source of great pride for our country," she wrote on X, alongside a picture of Antonelli holding the Italian flag.
 La Gazzetta dello Sport newspaper ran the headline "Kimitico", a play on words meaning "Legendary Kimi".
 La Stampa newspaper struck a similar tone, with its headline "Kimi nella leggenda" ("Kimi makes history.") 
 In Rome, locals took delight in an Italian sporting success, with one comparing Antonelli to tennis champion Jannik Sinner.
 "They're two shining stars of Italian sport," said Daniela Bulgarini. "He seems like a good kid, very talented. Talent and hard work always pay off."
 Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli celebrates with an Italian flag on the podium after finishing third in the Mexico City Grand Prix and clinching the 2026 Formula 1 World Championship. (Photo: Reuters/Eloisa Sanchez)
 DESTINED FOR THE TOP
 Antonelli, who drives for Mercedes, is the son of a sports car racing father who took him to the track as a young boy.
 He was taken on by Mercedes as an 11-year-old karter when his potential as a Formula 1 driver was apparent.
 "After such a long time without an Italian winning, whether with Ferrari or with other teams, other constructors, it's certainly a great thing," said Giovanni, a worker in Rome.
 Several hundred fans watched a screening of the grand prix late on Sunday at the Checco Costa Museum at the Imola F1 race track.
 Although Imola is the home track of the Ferrari team, fans put that allegiance to one side to cheer for Antonelli whose third-place finish in Mexico was enough to seal the title.
 Another watch-party was held in a cinema in Bologna.
 The local Serie A soccer club joined in the celebrations, with a post on X reading "The whole of Bologna is proud of you".
